A Plex watchlist is read with the user's own Plex sign-in (once after this is enabled) or, when Settings → Media → Plex Watchlist allows it, through your Plex server owner's account for Plex friends who opt in.

settings.playHistory.watchedThresholdHel: Minimum percentage of media that must be played to count as "watched"
settings.playHistory.completionThreshold: Cumulative watch percentage across one viewing arc to count as a completion in "Popular on Server". Stricter than the per-session Watched threshold.
settings.playHistory.arcGapHelp: Sessions on the same media farther apart than this start a new viewing arc. A weekend chunked watch stays one arc; a months-later rewatch starts a new one.
settings.playHistory.pollingIntervalHelp: How often to check for active sessions (default: 5s). The live cadence comes from the PLAY_HISTORY_SYNC_INTERVAL environment variable and applies on container restart — saving here records the value but does not change it.
settings.playHistory.retentionHelp: Delete play history older than this many days. 0 = keep forever.
settings.playHistory.howBody: Play history is tracked automatically by polling your Plex and Jellyfin servers every few seconds for active sessions. No configuration is needed in Plex or Jellyfin — it uses the same server connection already configured above.
settings.watchGrade.graceHelp: How long after a request becomes available before it counts toward the grade. Requests still inside it are listed but never scored — watched or not — so recent requesters aren't judged early. Default {default}.
settings.watchGrade.windowHelp: Only requests fulfilled within this many days are graded, so a user's grade reflects recent habits. 30–3650, or 0 for no limit. Must be longer than the grace period. Default {default}.
settings.watchGrade.tvPercentHelp: Share of a season's regular-season episodes in the library that must be watched for full credit; fewer earns partial credit. Each season is scored on its own and the best one counts, so a finished season keeps its credit as later seasons arrive. Default {default}.
settings.watchGrade.otherViewersHelp: A request the requester didn't watch still counts as watched once this many other people have watched it since it was requested. Each counts as play history recorded them — a movie marked Watched, or a season's episodes to the share above — and someone with both a Plex and a Jellyfin login counts once. 1–100, or 0 to turn it off. Default {default}.
settings.watchGrade.cutoffsHelp: The watch rate a user needs for each letter; anything below D is an F. Each cutoff must be higher than the next. Defaults A {a}, B {b}, C {c}, D {d}.
settings.watchGrade.minRequestsHelp: Scored requests a user needs before a letter shows. Below it their watch rate is still shown, just without a letter, so one unwatched film can't stamp a new requester an F. 1–100. Default {default}.
settings.watchGrade.howBody: Each user is graded A–F on the share of their approved requests they went on to watch once those became available, by the cutoffs above, once enough requests count. Approving a title counts for everyone who requested it. Pending and declined requests never count, and neither does a request whose title nobody approved. A movie counts when it reaches the play history Watched threshold (half credit once a quarter of it is played), a show when the share of one season's episodes is watched, and any request counts once enough other people have watched it. The same title requested on two instances counts once. Only plays after the request count, and requests fulfilled before play history began recording aren't graded. Grades are shown to admins only and never block a request.
settings.watchGrade.previewHelp: Grades every requester with the values above and with the ones saved now, without saving anything.
settings.watchGrade.previewFeatureOff: Watch grades are turned off in Settings → Features, so there is nothing to preview.
settings.watchGrade.previewNoHistory: Watch grades need play history tracking on at least one media server, so there is nothing to preview.
settings.watchGrade.stale: The values changed since this preview — preview again to update it.

settings.media.heading: {label} — additional servers
settings.media.intro: Extra {label} servers (e.g. a friend's separate server, or a second library). Availability and activity are combined across every configured server of this type.
settings.media.restrictSignInHelp: Only accounts this server has already synced into Summonarr — or anyone who has signed in before — may sign in. Unchecking lets ANY valid account on this Jellyfin server sign in and create a Summonarr account (not recommended).
settings.media.pathPrefixesHelp: Library-folder prefix stripped from this server's file paths when matching them against other servers (bad-match detection, library diff). Blank inherits the main server's prefixes — set these only if this server's folder layout differs.
settings.media.restrictedHelp: Only users granted access to this server see its library as available. Leave off to combine it into everyone's availability, like the main server. Admins always see it.
settings.media.confirmRemove: Remove {name}? On Save this deletes its cached library items, its active sessions, and its stored URL + {token} (encrypted — not recoverable), and marks its media-server users departed.
settings.media.loadFailed: Couldn't load the current servers — saving is disabled so an empty list can't wipe them. Hit Refresh.

settings.section.general.title: General
settings.section.rateLimiting.title: Rate Limiting
settings.section.rateLimiting.descriptio: Maximum actions allowed per user within the time window.
settings.section.quotas.title: Quotas
settings.section.quotas.description: Limit how many requests each user can submit in a rolling time period. Admins and quota-exempt users are never restricted.
settings.section.deletionVotes.title: Deletion Votes
settings.section.deletionVotes.descripti: Users can vote to remove items from the library. When an item reaches the threshold, admins are notified.
settings.section.authentication.title: Authentication
settings.section.authentication.descript: Control which sign-in methods are available. External providers (Plex, Jellyfin, OIDC) are configured via environment variables.
settings.section.sessions.title: Sessions
settings.section.sessions.description: Control how long users stay logged in. The "Remember me" duration applies when users check that option at login.
settings.section.maintenance.title: Maintenance Mode
settings.section.maintenance.description: When enabled, non-admin users will see a maintenance page instead of the app.
settings.section.motd.title: Message of the Day
settings.section.motd.description: Optional popup shown to users once per session after login. Leave blank to disable.
settings.section.donations.title: Donations
settings.section.donations.description: Configure donation links shown to users on the Donate page.
settings.section.plex.description: Allow users shared with your Plex account to sign in with Plex.
settings.section.jellyfin.description: Sync your Jellyfin library to show availability badges on media.
settings.section.mediaInstances.title: Additional media servers
settings.section.mediaInstances.descript: Connect extra Plex/Jellyfin servers (e.g. a friend's separate server). Availability and activity are combined across every configured server of a type.
settings.section.playHistory.title: Play History
settings.section.playHistory.description: Track playback sessions from Plex and Jellyfin. Plex is followed live through its event stream and Jellyfin through a frequent poller — no media-server webhooks are needed.
settings.section.watchGrades.title: Watch Grades
settings.section.watchGrades.description: Grade users on whether they watch what they request, from play history. Shown to admins on the Users page and the request queue; turn it off in Features.
settings.section.libraryMatching.title: Library Matching
settings.section.libraryMatching.descrip: Configure how file paths are normalised when comparing Plex and Jellyfin libraries for bad-match detection.
settings.section.radarr.description: Automatically send approved movie requests to Radarr.
settings.section.radarr4k.description: A separate Radarr instance for 4K movies. Users with the “Request 4K” permission get a 4K request option.
settings.section.sonarr.description: Automatically send approved TV show requests to Sonarr.
settings.section.sonarr4k.description: A separate Sonarr instance for 4K TV. Users with the “Request 4K” permission get a 4K request option.
settings.section.arrInstances.title: Additional instances
settings.section.arrInstances.descriptio: Configure extra Radarr/Sonarr instances (e.g. a dedicated anime instance) beyond the default and 4K instances above.
settings.section.email.title: Email
settings.section.email.description: Send admins an email when a new request or issue is submitted. Saving will send a test email to your account.
settings.section.discordBot.title: Discord Bot
settings.section.discordBot.description: Allow Discord users to request media via slash commands using Discord's HTTP Interactions endpoint. No extra process or environment variables needed.
settings.section.iosPushRelay.title: iOS Push Relay
settings.section.iosPushRelay.descriptio: iOS push notifications reach the App Store app through the app publisher's APNs relay. It holds the app's Apple push key and can't be self-hosted, so leave the relay URL blank. The relay never sees titles or usernames. Add a relay key if you were issued one, and optionally recommend a minimum app build.
settings.section.externalRatings.title: External Ratings
settings.section.externalRatings.descrip: Adds IMDb, Rotten Tomatoes, RT Audience, Metacritic, and Trakt ratings to media pages. MDBList is recommended — it covers TV shows and adds Audience scores.
settings.section.ipGeolocation.title: IP Geolocation
settings.section.ipGeolocation.descripti: Resolves stream IPs to city, ISP, and approximate location on the activity pages, similar to Tautulli's IP info popup.
settings.section.webhooks.title: Webhooks
settings.section.webhooks.description: Add these URLs in Radarr/Sonarr → Settings → Connect → Webhook so requests are marked Available the moment a download completes.
settings.section.scheduledJobs.title: Scheduled Jobs
settings.section.scheduledJobs.descripti: Background cron jobs and their current status. Click Run to trigger on demand.
settings.section.auditLog.title: Audit Log
settings.section.auditLog.description: How long audit rows keep IP addresses, devices, and user names before the daily scrub redacts them. A manual “Scrub PII” button lives on the Audit Log page.
settings.section.dbMetrics.title: DB Metrics
settings.section.dbMetrics.description: Read-only snapshot of database row counts.
settings.metrics.requests.heading: Requests
settings.metrics.users.heading: Users
settings.metrics.issues.heading: Issues
settings.metrics.libraryCache.heading: Library Cache
settings.metrics.tmdbCore.heading: TmdbMediaCore
settings.metrics.tmdbCore.description: Normalised metadata table (title, poster, year, rating) used by all grid pages to avoid live TMDB calls. Populated automatically as pages are browsed; use Initial DB Fill to seed it immediately.
settings.metrics.playHistory.heading: Play History
settings.featureDesc.integration_webhook: Send request and issue events to the webhook, ntfy and Gotify channels configured under Settings → Notifications.
settings.section.notificationAgents.desc: Forward request, issue and download events to your own services. Each channel picks the events it receives; failed deliveries are retried three times.
settings.section.plexWatchlist.title: Plex Watchlist
settings.section.plexWatchlist.descripti: How watchlist auto-request reads Plex watchlists. A user's own Plex sign-in is always used when there is one; these switches add your Plex server owner's account as a second way in.
settings.form.plexWatchlistServer.title: Read friends' watchlists through the server owner
settings.form.plexWatchlistServer.help: Users who never signed in with Plex are read with the Plex admin token when they are your server's Plex friends and their watchlist is visible to friends. Each user switches it on in their profile.
settings.form.plexWatchlistAutoEnroll.he: Also read every permitted friend who has not switched auto-request off, even if they never opened Summonarr. Off by default: requests filed for people who did not ask for them can surprise them.
settings.plexWatchlist.status.never: The server-owner path has not run yet.
settings.plexWatchlist.status.summary: Last run {time}: {ok} connected, {private} private, {error} failed; {unmatched} Plex friends have no Summonarr account.
settings.section.request4k.title: 4K Requests
settings.section.request4k.description: Who may request 4K versions once a 4K Radarr or Sonarr instance is configured above.
settings.arr.removedOpenRequests: Open requests still target removed {label} instances: {list}. They can't be approved or sent until they are declined or requested again.
